# nonRegExp

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** a regular expression.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonRegExp() — Checks whether a value is **not** a regular expression. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonRegExp<T>(value: T | RegExp): value is T;
```

`nonRegExp(value)` is the same test as `!isRegExp(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

Identified by its internal tag rather than by `instanceof`, so a regular expression from another frame is recognised too.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type          | Description         |
| :-------- | :------------ | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| RegExp` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not a regular expression; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonRegExp("/a/"); // => true
nonRegExp({}); // => true
nonRegExp(null); // => true
nonRegExp(/a/); // => false
nonRegExp(new RegExp("a")); // => false
```
